Let
\[
p(t)=\prod_{k=0}^2(1-\alpha_k t).
\]
Since \(A=\operatorname{diag}(1,2,4)\), after three steps the three coordinate multipliers are \(p(1),p(2),p(4)\). For \(x_0\) uniform on the unit sphere in \(\mathbb R^3\),
\[
\mathbb E(x_{0,i}^2)=\frac13,
\]
so
\[
R(\alpha_0,\alpha_1,\alpha_2)
=\frac13\left(p(1)^2+p(2)^2+p(4)^2\right).
\]

Set
\[
z_k=1-4\alpha_k.
\]
Because \(0<\alpha_k\le \frac12\), we have \(-1\le z_k<1\), and
\[
1-\alpha_k=\frac{3+z_k}{4},\qquad
1-2\alpha_k=\frac{1+z_k}{2},\qquad
1-4\alpha_k=z_k.
\]
Thus, writing \(F=3R\),
\[
F=\frac{\prod(3+z_k)^2}{4096}
+\frac{\prod(1+z_k)^2}{64}
+\prod z_k^2.
\]
Drop the nonnegative middle term and put \(x_k=|z_k|\). Since \(3+z_k\ge 3-x_k\),
\[
F\ge \frac{\prod(3-x_k)^2}{4096}+\prod x_k^2.
\]
Let \(u=x_0x_1x_2\). For \(x,y\in[0,1]\),
\[
(3-x)(3-y)-2(3-xy)=3(1-x)(1-y)\ge0.
\]
Applying this twice gives
\[
\prod_{k=0}^2(3-x_k)\ge 4(3-u).
\]
Therefore
\[
F\ge \frac{16(3-u)^2}{4096}+u^2
=\frac{(3-u)^2}{256}+u^2.
\]
This convex quadratic is minimized when
\[
-\frac{3-u}{128}+2u=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
u=\frac3{257}.
\]
At that value,
\[
F_{\min}=\frac{(768/257)^2}{256}+\left(\frac3{257}\right)^2
=\frac{2304+9}{257^2}
=\frac9{257}.
\]

Equality is attained, for example, by
\[
z_0=z_1=-1,\qquad z_2=-\frac3{257},
\]
i.e.
\[
\alpha_0=\alpha_1=\frac12,\qquad
\alpha_2=\frac{65}{257}.
\]
Then \(p(2)=0\), and the bound above is sharp. Hence
\[
R_*=\frac13F_{\min}=\boxed{\frac3{257}}.
\]
